scenes.heading: Testing Data Pipelines in CI
scenes.subheading: Catch data bugs before they reach production
scenes.narration: Testing data pipelines in continuous integration catches broken logic and bad data before it ever reaches production.

scenes.heading: Layers of data testing
bullets: Schema tests for column types and nullability
Data quality tests: uniqueness, ranges, referential integrity
Integration tests running the pipeline end to end
scenes.narration: The first layer is unit tests around individual transformation functions, verifying logic in isolation. Schema tests then confirm that columns have the expected types and nullability. Data quality tests assert business rules such as uniqueness, acceptable value ranges, and referential integrity. Finally, integration tests run the pipeline end to end against sample data to prove the pieces fit together.

scenes.heading: The testing pyramid for data
scenes.narration: Think of a pyramid: many fast unit tests form the base and run in seconds. Above them sit schema and contract tests that guard the shape of your data. Data quality assertions come next, checking the actual values. At the top, a few slower end-to-end runs on fixture data validate the whole pipeline, kept few because they are the most expensive.

scenes.heading: dbt tests in a CI job
scenes.code:
# schema.yml
models:
  - name: orders
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        tests:
          - unique
          - not_null
      - name: status
        tests:
          - accepted_values:
              values: ['open', 'shipped', 'closed']
      - name: customer_id
        tests:
          - relationships:
              to: ref('customers')
              field: customer_id
scenes.narration: This dbt schema file declares tests directly alongside the model. The order id must be both unique and never null, catching duplicate or missing keys. The status column is restricted to a fixed set of accepted values, so an unexpected status fails the build. And the relationships test enforces referential integrity by requiring every customer id to exist in the customers model. In CI, any failing assertion turns the pipeline red.

scenes.heading: Test in prod vs test in CI
scenes.narration: When you only discover problems in production, bad data reaches dashboards, stakeholder trust erodes, and you pay for costly incident response. Testing in CI catches those failures before merge, so bad data never ships and fixes stay cheap and fast.

scenes.text: Layer unit, schema, quality, and integration tests in CI so every change proves its correctness before it merges.
scenes.narration: Layer unit, schema, quality, and integration tests in your CI pipeline so that every change must prove its correctness before it is allowed to merge.
